newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Somali faction appeals for aid for drought victims.
newsitem.headline: Somali faction appeals for aid for drought victims.

text.p: A Somali faction led by Hussein Aideed appealed on Monday for international aid for drought victims in southwestern Somalia, saying the lack of rains was a national disaster.

Mohamed Kanyare Afrah, interior minister in a government appointed by Aideed but without international recognition, said people and livestock in the southwest had started dying from famine and thirst.
He appealed for water tankers and food for the southwest and also said it had not rained in parts of central Somalia for two years. "It's a national disaster," he told a news conference.
The U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) and Food and Agriculture Organisation forecast in December the secondary crop in southern regions of maize and sorghum would be about 45 percent less than average.
It said livestock prices in the southwest had fallen and cereal prices had increased and if the secondary rainy season failed then herders who had lost livestock would require some food aid.

Last month, a WFP technical group reported that some food assistance might soon be needed in Gedo region in the southwest while in the south and central regions the situation could deteriorate if a lack of rain persisted.

A shortage of water for pastoralists in much of barren Somalia is an annual problem, forcing them to move livestock to other areas during the dry season. Some 300,000 people were killed by famine fuelled by civil war in Somalia in 1992.
